description: Shared crypto provider corpus. Read byte-for-byte by @kokuin/crypto-conformance (TypeScript) and crates/kokuin-crypto/tests/corpus.rs (Rust). All byte strings are lowercase hex. `weakenedBy` names the deliberately weakened verifiers, per backend, that ACCEPT a rejected vector: the self-tests on each side assert that removing exactly that guard flips exactly the listed vectors, so no vector is confounded by a second check. An empty list means no single-guard removal flips the vector in that backend; the note explains why.

verify.name: Ed25519 RFC 8032 test 1 over a mutated message
Ed25519 S >= L
verify.note: RFC 8032 test 1 with S replaced by S + L. A verifier that reduces S mod L accepts it; both backends require canonical S.

verify.name: Ed25519 mixed-order public key, k = 3 mod 4
verify.note: A = B + T (T the order-4 point, encoded as 32 zero bytes), R = B, S = 1 + k mod L, k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L = 3 mod 4. Satisfies the cofactored equation only. Noble verifies cofactored, so its subgroup check on A is the sole rejecting guard. Rust (dalek verify_strict) verifies cofactorless and [k]T != 0, so the equation itself rejects it even without the subgroup guard; only a cofactored Rust check accepts it.

verify.name: Ed25519 mixed-order signature point
verify.note: A = B, R = B + T, S = 1 + k mod L. Satisfies the cofactored equation only. Noble's subgroup check on R is the sole rejecting guard. In Rust a torsion component in R can never satisfy the cofactorless equation when A is torsion-free, so the R guard is not independently reachable there; only a cofactored Rust check accepts it.

verify.name: Ed25519 mixed-order public key, k = 0 mod 4
verify.note: A = B + T, R = B, message "m0", S = 1 + k mod L with k = 0 mod 4, so [k]T = 0 and the cofactorless equation also holds. dalek verify_strict accepts it (A is not small-order), so this is the vector that certifies the Rust subgroup guard on A. Noble's subgroup check on A is likewise the sole rejecting guard.

verify.name: Ed25519 identity public key and R with S = 0
verify.note: Small-order forgery valid under both equations for every message. Noble rejects it three times over (subgroup checks on A and R, and noble's own small-order check), and Rust twice (strict point guard and verify_strict's weak-key check), so no single guard removal flips it in either backend; an unguarded cofactored Rust check accepts it.

verify.name: Ed25519 non-canonical identity encodings
verify.note: A and R encode y = p + 1, a non-canonical identity, with S = 0. Every non-canonical Ed25519 encoding (y in [p, 2^255)) decodes to a point that is small-order or not torsion-free, so the canonical-encoding check is never the sole guard in either backend; a Rust cofactored check with lenient decoding accepts it.

verify.name: ES256 compact low-S
verify.note: Raw message hashed once with SHA-256; a double-hashing verifier rejects it.

verify.name: ES256 compact low-S over a mutated message
ES256 high-S
verify.note: The valid signature with s replaced by n - s.

verify.name: ES256 small scalars r = 5, s = 1
verify.note: X is the P-256 point with the smallest x (5), Q = r^-1 (s X - h G). Valid; the base for the r >= n and s >= n vectors, which need r and s below 2^256 - n.

verify.name: ES256 r >= n
verify.note: r = n + 5, s = 1. A verifier that reduces r mod n accepts it.

verify.name: ES256 s >= n
verify.note: r = 5, s = n + 1. A verifier that reduces s mod n accepts it.

verify.name: ES256 r = 0 with valid s
verify.note: Rejected by the range check and, without it, by the ECDSA equation (u2 = 0 leaves X = u1 G, whose x is not 0). Pins agreement on rejecting rather than throwing; no single guard removal flips it.

verify.name: ES256 s = 0 with valid r
verify.note: Rejected by the range check; s has no inverse, and a verifier treating 0^-1 as 0 reaches the point at infinity, whose x (0) differs from r. No single guard removal flips it.

verify.name: ES256 r = s = 0
verify.note: CVE-2022-21449 shape: a verifier without the non-zero check that computes s^-1 as s^(n-2) and reads the point at infinity as x = 0 accepts it for every key and message. Only the noble self-test implements that weakened verifier.
